notes: Changed rule, graded against the current text: Chain fallible steps with `with`. Its one-step paragraph now adds "This holds in a public function whose only fallible call is the first step and whose body builds the result: the `with` saves the error clause and costs the reader a search for steps that are not there." (idiomatic-elixir/SKILL.md, under the rule heading). Violating runs out of 5 per sentence: one-step opening sentence ("A `with` has at least two `<-` steps; one step is a `case`.") 2, opus-1 and haiku-2; new public-function sentence 1, opus-1, whose commented controller action export/2 (lines 223-227) is a public function with one `<-` step on its only fallible call, MyApp.RateLimiter.check/1, plus an `else`, so the new sentence and the opening sentence both decide it; haiku-2's `with {:ok, term} <- read_term(path), do: validate(term)` (line 159) is a defp, so the unchanged opening sentence decides it, and its body returns validate/1, a second fallible call, without chaining it. Nested-case clause 0. Else sentence (unchanged) 1, haiku-1: its four-step with (lines 181-189) has an else whose `{:ok, other} -> {:error, {:invalid_shape, other}}` relabels the second step's pattern mismatch as an error and whose `{:error, reason} -> {:error, reason}` is a no-op; the previous sweep left a one-clause rewrap and an else where "nothing is relabelled" clean, but here a step's outcome is mapped back to an error in the else instead of in decode/1, the shape the rule's "Instead of" example shows, so it is counted. Sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 have no with and are not exercised.

The other changes since db91c23 (the new `do:` rule, the captures rule, and Assert with patterns in testing.md) are not in this case's list and decide nothing here. Branch, Naming, Comments and the five process rules are unchanged and graded to the 2026-10-22 standard: an `if` on one boolean condition is clean and `unless` is counted (sonnet-2 line 155; the rule says "Do not use `unless`, which is deprecated"); single-letter n is counted under Naming (opus-1 lines 154 and 162), as the previous sweep counted n in baseline-sonnet-1, while ts, acc, term and binary are not; section-label comments (## Public API, # Client API, ## Helpers) and a start_link/1 or child_spec/1 without @doc are not counted under Comments; a configuration file read in init/1 is a missed case check but no verdict rests on it; haiku-2's three-element {:error, :rate_limited, retry_after_ms} return is not counted; a `case` nested in an `if` branch (sonnet-1 lines 92-96, sonnet-2 lines 100-104) is listed under Keep functions short, as the previous sweep listed opus-1's if inside a case there, and not under Branch, since the outer `if` tests one boolean and the inner construct is a `case`.

Designs: opus-1 keeps per-user per-second counter buckets in a public ordered_set ETS table owned by the GenServer; callers increment with :ets.update_counter/4, sum the last 61 buckets with :ets.select/2 and decrement their own bucket when over, so Pick the abstraction, Use ETS and Keep each process behind one module are clean, as in the previous sweep's opus baseline; it again hard-codes name: __MODULE__ (line 71) and fixed table names (lines 58-59), so the responsive rule is violated. The other four runs keep every count in GenServer state behind GenServer.call, so Pick the abstraction and Use ETS are violated in all four, as in the previous sweep. Both Haiku runs use the top-level module RateLimiter (line 1), so Naming is violated for both.

Each file was formatted, compiled and run in a scratch copy. mix format --check-formatted passes for opus-1, haiku-1, haiku-2 and sonnet-2 and fails for sonnet-1 (line 98, 99 characters); no session ran mix format. All five compile with elixirc --warnings-as-errors; opus-1's example callers are comments this time, so its whole file compiles. In every run a 50-task concurrent burst for one user admitted exactly 2 at a default limit of 2, and an injected expired entry was removed by the sweep while live users were kept. A second instance under name: :other started and admitted 2 of 50 in haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2; in opus-1 it returned {:error, {:already_started, pid}}.

Correctness defects outside the graded rules: haiku-2's moduledoc gives the limits file in Elixir syntax (%{default: 60, users: %{...}}., lines 15-21), which :file.consult/1 reads as an Erlang comment, so a file written as documented fails start with {:invalid_rate_limit_config, path, :expected_single_term}; the same data in Erlang syntax (#{default => 2, ...}.) works and the 5-limit override admitted 5 of 50. Sonnet-2 documents {"user-42", 600}. (line 15), which :file.consult/1 reads with a charlist key, so a string user id never matches its override and gets the default (an override of 5 admitted 2 of 50). Haiku-1 looks the limit up by to_string(user_id) (line 144) but keys counts by the raw id (line 151), so 7 and "7" each get the full limit.

All five runs have rc 0, a model_id matching their tier and empty reads; each transcript mentions Skill only in the tool list, and no session called it. Expected reads (processes.md) is unmet in all five, as expected for baseline runs told not to invoke skills.
